02 / THE FORMULAS

Show your workings

The arithmetic behind the plan, with your current numbers filled in.

01 / STITCH COUNT

Size the tube

Apply negative ease to the measured foot circumference, multiply by stitch gauge, then round to the nearest multiple of four.

stitches = round₄(circumference × (1 − ease) × sts / cm)
02 / HEEL

Divide in half

The heel works over half the tube. For a classic flap, work roughly one row per heel stitch and pick up one stitch for every two flap rows.

heel sts = total ÷ 2
pickups / side = flap rows ÷ 2
03 / TOE

Shape the wedge

Begin or finish with about a quarter of the tube stitches. Change by four stitches per shaping round. Shape rapidly to half the tube, then every other round to full width (reverse for cuff-down).

toe length ≈ total toe rounds ÷ rounds per cm
04 / LANDMARKS

Find the turn

For a toe-up flap, increase about ⅜ of the heel stitches on each side over alternate rounds. For Fish Lips Kiss, the toe-up allowance is an editable starting estimate; the designer’s foot template is the fitting method.

gusset length ≈ (increases / side × 2) ÷ rounds per cm

Notes & sources

Size presets are examples, not shoe-size standards. This calculator assumes stockinette gauge and a 10% ease default; adjust for yarn, stitch pattern, and personal fit. Toe and gusset lengths are estimates because your knitting and heel turn can change the finished length.

The Knitty sizing guide discusses sock ease. Knitty’s heel-flap guide covers slipped edges and pickup spacing. Fish Lips Kiss is by Sox Therapist; use the original pattern for its full heel method.
